security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and instructional text in SKILL.md. I found no executable commands, prompt injection attempts, data exfiltration intent, or system reconnaissance behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid overlap with other skills' trigger conditions

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 26-30 are a Markdown code fence showing an example directory tree. No executable command or shell invocation is present.
Lines 30-34 only close and reopen Markdown formatting around documentation headings. This is not Ruby backtick execution.
Lines 34-45 are a Markdown code fence containing an example file tree. It documents optional files and does not execute commands.
Lines 45-61 are surrounding Markdown documentation and a YAML example fence. There is no runtime shell execution path.
Lines 61-63 are a fenced YAML documentation example for a description field. The backticks are Markdown syntax, not executable code.
Line 84 advises authors to avoid overlapping trigger conditions with other skills. It does not inspect the system or collect host information.

content.user_title: Create Claude Code Skills From a Reference Template
content.value_statement: Building a Claude Code skill can be unclear when the required structure is new. This reference skill explains files, frontmatter, triggers, and authoring patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md file for a plugin skill.
Shows optional supporting folders for references, examples, and scripts.
Lists frontmatter fields used by Claude Code skills.
Provides a sample description pattern for skill activation.
Summarizes practical guidelines for focused skill content.
limitations: It is a documentation reference, not an automated scaffold generator.
It does not validate skill packages or marketplace metadata.
It does not include runnable helper scripts.
It gives general patterns rather than domain-specific skill logic.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Format

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Skill Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Use example-skill to help draft a clear trigger description for a skill about my topic.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Skill Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use example-skill to compare my skill outline against the expected files, frontmatter, and content sections.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Skill Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Use example-skill to propose a focused skill package structure with references, examples, and scripts only where needed.

output_examples.input: Explain what files my first skill needs.
output_examples.output: A concise explanation of the required SKILL.md file, plus optional folders for references, examples, and helper scripts.

output_examples.input: Help me improve a skill description.
output_examples.output: A clearer trigger description that names user phrases, keywords, and the topic area the skill should cover.

output_examples.input: Review whether my skill is too broad.
output_examples.output: A focused review of purpose, activation conditions, content organization, and overlap with nearby skills.

best_practices: Use specific trigger phrases that match real user requests.
Keep each skill focused on one clear domain.
Add reference files only when they make the main skill easier to use.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague descriptions that can activate for unrelated tasks.
Do not mix several unrelated domains into one skill.
Do not add helper scripts unless the skill clearly needs them.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps authors understand the structure and writing patterns for Claude Code plugin skills.

faq.question: Does it generate files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for authors who are creating skill files.

faq.question: Can it help with frontmatter?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common frontmatter fields and explains the role of the description field.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The source content is focused on Claude Code plugin skills, but the marketplace lists Claude and Codex compatibility.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on skill structure, activation descriptions, and content organization.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when planning, documenting, or reviewing the structure of a plugin skill.
